html:
The Viceroyalty of Peru was the Spanish government of South America, ruled by a viceroy in Lima. Spain created it in 1542, a decade after Francisco Pizarro conquered the Inca Empire, and for two centuries it covered almost all of Spanish South America. It was one of the two great halves of Spanish America.

Its wealth was silver. The mountain of Potosí in today's Bolivia was worked by Andean men drafted under the mita, an Inca labour duty that the Viceroy Francisco de Toledo turned into forced mine work in the 1570s. Silver went by sea to Panama and on to Spain.

In the 1700s Spain cut it down, splitting off the Viceroyalty of New Granada in the north and the Río de la Plata in the south. The great Andean revolt of Túpac Amaru II in 1780 was crushed. Peru was the royalist stronghold in the wars of independence and fell last, after the Battle of Ayacucho in 1824.
